Our Legacy

O-Sensei Steve Reynolds

1948 — 2022. For well over 50 years, a respected practitioner and instructor whose curriculum is still taught exactly as he built it.

Boyhood

Steve Reynolds begins his martial arts journey studying Kung Fu as a boy in Newfoundland.

Military Years

Continues his training in the Canadian military, exposed to several martial art styles, and tests his skill while serving with NATO forces in West Germany.

Return to Canada

Studies with the fledgling Canadian Jiu-Jitsu Association under Prof. Ronald W. Forrester, networking with senior martial artists including Prof. Wally Jay and Hanshi Richard Kim.

October 1973

Opens his own dojo in Richmond Hill — originally the Richmond Hill Jiu-Jitsu Academy, later the Richmond Hill Jiu-Jitsu Kai.

Early Tournaments

O-Sensei Reynolds is part of a pioneering group of Jiu-Jitsu black belts sent to local karate tournaments to help develop the rules that became modern Sport Jiu-Jitsu.

Later Years

The name Kitsune Ryu is formally adopted for the dojo's own system, built on ten original katas developed by O-Sensei himself.

1948 – 2022

O-Sensei Steve Reynolds passes, leaving behind over 50 years of instruction, a curriculum still taught today, and the motto: Honour Above All.

Competition History

Honour on the mat.

Our dojo started competing through karate tournaments. O-Sensei Reynolds was part of a pioneering group of Jiu-Jitsu black belts sent out to local karate tournaments to investigate how the sparring worked, and eventually to help develop the rules for what has since evolved into Sport Jiu-Jitsu.

Because of that early participation, Jiu-Jitsu fighters were accepted into open-style karate tournaments in kata, weapons, and kumite. O-Sensei's friendships with the senior karate instructors of the day paved the way for what we still do — many of the tournaments our students attend today are a continuation of friendships formed in the early 1970s.

Over the years, the Richmond Hill Budokan has produced World Champions, Martial Arts Hall of Fame recipients, and students who've gone on to movie and TV appearances — always in service of the same standard: honour in showing our craft, and honing our skills to keep improving.
